title: My first weeks
text:
My first weeks at UBC involved getting familiar with a broad set of tools. I have been working with Python, R, JupyterLab, Git, GitHub, and the Bash terminal. Although I have used computational tools in engineering research, learning how these tools fit together into a consistent workflow has brought new challenges.
One practical lesson has been that writing code is only part of the work. Running a notebook from beginning to end, rendering a document, and keeping track of changes all require attention. Setting up this website has helped me connect several of these steps: editing source files, previewing the result, and recording changes with Git.
As the program continues, I hope to become more confident with these workflows and spend more time exploring the questions they can help answer. I am especially interested in connections between NLP, earthquake engineering, earthquake seismology, and seismic hazards. For now, this website gives me a place to document what I am learning and reflect on my progress.

title: About
text: My academic background is in civil and earthquake engineering. My doctoral research examines how buildings respond to earthquakes and how analytical predictions relate to damage observed in the field. This work combines structural modelling, numerical simulations, and field measurements, and has strengthened my interest in extracting useful insights from complex data.

title: About
text:
Why data science
Working with research data has motivated me to develop more systematic approaches to programming, analysis, and reproducibility. I believe natural language processing brings together my interests in analytical problem-solving and language. I am particularly interested in exploring how machine learning and NLP can support engineering research, including working with information contained in technical documents. I am currently looking to the possibility of applying NLP to probablistic seismic hazard analysis to develop strategies for better understanding and more adequate preparedness toward impending future earthquakes.

title: About

Outside of data science
Outside my studies, I enjoy working out, martial arts, and exploring languages. Poetry and literature are also important interests of mine. Learning languages gives me another way to engage with different perspectives and balances the technical focus of my research. About this site

title: Behtash Javidsharifi (AKA James Javid)
text:
Welcome! My background is in civil engineering. My PhD-level research focused on empirical approaches to earthquake damage correlation. I have developed an interest in data science, and I am working hard to quench it! My interests connect structural engineering, languages, machine learning, and natural language processing. I hope to strengthen my computational skills and apply them to interdisciplinary research and practical problems.
